description:
## Songs play again when you are signed in

Signing in could leave the app unable to play anything at all — every song refused with *Video unavailable*, while signing out fixed it. Four separate faults were behind that, and all four are fixed.

- **Signing in no longer breaks playback.** The identity that says who is asking was being saved empty, because it is filled in a moment after the sign-in page closes and nothing waited for it.
- **A stale identity now mends itself.** When it expires the catalogue stops answering — every song, every source — which is why reinstalling helped and nothing else did. It is replaced in place now, without the reinstall.
- **The two spare ways of unscrambling a stream address work again.** They depend on a component that was never handed anything to fetch with, so both had been quietly returning nothing for every song.
- **The app no longer asks for a stream it cannot unscramble.** It was naming a version of the site's player it had no way of reading, which guaranteed a refusal on a step that reported no error.

## Less waiting

- **The next song is ready before the gap.** Its address is fetched while the current song is still playing, so the handover has no pause in it. A song that took up to thirteen seconds to start now starts immediately.
- **A refused stream is spotted in one request instead of a failed load.** The check now asks exactly what the player is about to ask, so when the first source will not serve a song the app moves to one that will in about four seconds rather than thirteen.
- **Loudness levelling is ready when the song starts** rather than being fetched again over the opening bars.

## Updates, from inside the app

Knowing a new version existed was as far as this went before — what followed was a web page, a list of files, a guess at which one, and an archive to find and make sense of.

- **A new version is offered when you open the app**, once, with the notes attached — and not again until the next one.
- **Settings → Updater → Check for updates** asks on demand and downloads it for you, with progress.
- **The download goes to your Downloads folder**, so it is still there if you have to uninstall first, and it says so when that is the case rather than leaving you with *App not installed*.
- The updater had also been asking a repository that isn't this one, reading a release's version from its headline instead of its tag, and looking for filenames this project never publishes. Any one of those was enough to make it find nothing.

## Also

- The changelog you are reading now travels inside the app, so it is here whether or not there is a connection.
- The *update available* badge on the About page no longer stays on permanently.
